To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetic basis of root system architecture (RSA), which contributes to nitrogen (n) uptake and utilization, was investigated in a germplasm-enhancement of a maize double haploid (DH) population of 226 DH lines using a genome-wide-association study (GWAS) under two N conditions.
we used genome-wide association studies to identify the genetic basis of root system architecture under high and low nitrogen conditions in a maize germplasm enhancement population.
we performed GWAS to identify SNPs associated with RSA in a maize DH population under two nitrogen conditions, and identified 33 and 53 significant SNPs under high and low nitrogen conditions.

the genetic control of RSA traits under two nitrogen levels in maize.
the genetic architecture of RSA traits under two N conditions in maize, and provides valuable information for the genetic dissection of the genetic basis for RSA traits in maize.
the genetic basis of root system architecture under two nitrogen levels, and the results will provide a reference for the molecular breeding of root traits in maize.

the GWAS results of RSA under different N conditions can be used as a reference for the genetic basis of maize RSA and the candidate genes identified in this study will be useful for further understanding of the genetics of RSA in maize.

the GWAS analysis identified a number of SNPs and candidate genes associated with RSA traits under high and low nitrogen conditions.
